name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.298.0 — workspace-scan.js now emits one {root, stack, manifest} row per (directory, stack) pair instead of the first manifest only, so a polyglot root (package.json beside pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml …) gets /spec:enforce cells for every stack. Manifests of one stack still collapse to one row; single-stack output is unchanged. Re-run /spec:enforce on polyglot hosts to pick up the missing stacks. 7.297.0 — review legs reuse a whole-suite gate as the suite leg — gateRunsSuite in lib/gate-resolve.js proves the host gate already ran the full test command (no {testDirs}/{scopeDirs}, a && segment equal to testCommand), so review-legs and --mark closed skip the redundant suite run; a scoped gate behaves as before, and every legs run now records wall-clock milliseconds per leg. 7.296.0 — the host declares its file shapes: grounding contract gains the optional fileShapes block (testGlobs, codeExtensions, manifests over stack-neutral defaults in lib/file-shapes.js); every script classifies tests, code and manifests through it; /spec:init profiles and writes the block and /spec:doctor check 1 proves each declared test glob with init-gen shapes-check.
